first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it because Mauritius is on our list and she wanted to know whether the civil side would dictate the schedule. The first screen answers the question and doesn't gush. There's no price and no 'affordable'. But it's a paperwork guide for two Australians organising it themselves. Her summary would be 'clear on the legal order, says nothing about scale or privacy'. I'd read the takeaways, the Port Louis visit, the ceremony and resort sections, and the close.

journey.reaction: Good. Two words, no hedging. That's the tone I want from someone advising us.

journey.quote: A Mauritius wedding is legally binding for two Australians when it follows the Civil Status Division's process for two non-citizens.
journey.reaction: We're split between Dubai, Sydney and London. The whole page assumes two Australian passports and an Australian registry. My assistant would have to work out what applies to us.

journey.quote: Some couples keep the civil marriage small and early in the day, with only their witnesses, then gather everyone on the sand at dusk for the vows they have written.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful idea on the page for us. A private legal ceremony with only family, kept away from 300 guests and their phones, and the big ceremony later. That's exactly how I'd want it.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Look at your guests' routes as well as your own, particularly anyone combining the wedding with an African itinerary.
journey.reaction: Someone who thinks about the guests' travel, not just ours. With guests coming from several continents, that matters.

journey.section: What the Civil Status Division asks for
journey.quote: Order fresh birth certificates from your state or territory registry once the date is fixed, not a year ahead when the planning feels exciting.
journey.reaction: The timing tip is useful, but 'when the planning feels exciting' is a bit chatty. It's written for a couple doing their own admin, and my assistant does ours.

journey.quote: Put this visit at the start of the trip, before the welcome drinks and the spa days.
journey.reaction: This is planner thinking. It fits the legal step into a wedding week instead of just repeating the government page.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: Treat the Officer's transport as part of the run sheet, with a car, a driver and a named person who meets them at the gate.
journey.reaction: A named person at the gate is the kind of detail our security team would ask about. This line sounds like someone who has run a controlled event.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach or at your resort
journey.quote: Does a ceremony on the beach itself need any permission, and who arranges it?
journey.reaction: Fine, but this is the list of questions for the resort, and the ones I'd actually ask are missing: can the beach and the property be closed to the public, can we take the whole resort, and how does their security work with ours?

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach or at your resort
journey.quote: If you offer a wedding package, what exactly does it include for the civil formalities, and what sits outside it?
journey.reaction: I understand it's a question for the resort, but 'package' twice in a few paragraphs makes the whole thing feel like a standard offer. We wouldn't be buying a package.

journey.quote: January and February are the warmest months, with the average day maximum reaching 29.2 degrees Celsius.
journey.reaction: Too many numbers. Tell me which months work and which coast, and leave the averages out.

journey.quote: Put repellent out for the evening ceremony and reception.
journey.reaction: That's what a venue team does without being told. Telling me makes the page feel aimed at couples who've never hosted anything.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One point of contact suits me, because fewer people means fewer leaks. 'Inclusions' still sounds a little like a package.

journey.section: Plan your Mauritius wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing is right for my family office. AUD and 'your time zone' assume I'm sitting in Sydney.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a Mauritius wedding for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee worked out, and do you earn commission from the resorts you book? (deferred business detail)
Who would actually be on the ground in Mauritius for us during the wedding week? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private transfers and airport handling for us and our guests? (deferred business detail)
What access or perks come with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
Would you handle the Civil Status Office submission and the Port Louis visit for us, or are we expected to do it ourselves? (deferred business detail)
Can a Mauritius resort be taken over exclusively for several days, with the beach in front closed to the public, and can our own security work with the venue's?
Does the process differ if one of us is not Australian, or if our family members acting as witnesses hold other passports?
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, guest lists, no social media?
Can I work through my assistant or family office, and can you quote in another currency?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you offer a wedding package, what exactly does it include for the civil formalities, and what sits outside it?
turn_offs_found.why: Package language. Even aimed at the resort, it frames the wedding as a standard product, which is the thing I fear most from a planner.

turn_offs_found.quote: Put repellent out for the evening ceremony and reception.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Advice this basic makes the page read as written for first-timers, not for someone hiring a premium planner.

turn_offs_found.quote: Order fresh birth certificates from your state or territory registry once the date is fixed, not a year ahead when the planning feels exciting.
turn_offs_found.why: 'When the planning feels exciting' is an eager, chatty touch in an otherwise assured page.

would_share_with: My assistant might keep the Port Louis timing and the private civil ceremony idea for the planning file. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mauritius-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public link on a blog post. I'd want a private introduction and some sign you've done this at our size and keep it quiet. The legal guidance is solid and the run-sheet details show some experience, but nothing here speaks to exclusive use, security or discretion.

top_3_changes: In 'Ceremonies on the beach or at your resort', add one generic question to the resort list: whether the ceremony space or the whole property can be reserved for exclusive use and closed to the public, and how the venue's security works alongside a private team. Write it as a question to ask, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.

Reword 'If you offer a wedding package, what exactly does it include for the civil formalities, and what sits outside it?' to something like 'What exactly is included for the civil formalities, and what sits outside it?', so the page uses 'package' less.

Trim the over-explaining: cut 'Put repellent out for the evening ceremony and reception.', drop 'when the planning feels exciting', and reduce the climate averages to the seasons and the wettest and driest months.
